question: A standard Rubik’s cube has been broken into cubes making up its sides. The cubes are jumbled, and one is removed. There are 6 cubes with one colored face, 12 edge cubes with two colored faces, and 8 corner cubes with three colored faces. All blue cubes have been found. All cubes directly left, right, above, and below the orange center cube have been found, along with the center cube. The green corners have all been found, along with all green that borders yellow. For all orange cubes found, the opposite face’s cubes have been found. The removed cube has two colors on its faces. What are they? Answer using a comma separated list, with the colors ordered alphabetically.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Team assembled: Assistant (reasoning and tools), WebSurfer (web lookup), FileSurfer (diagramming). Plan: 1) Fix a standard color orientation and opposites. 2) Translate constraints into a checklist of which edge cubies are guaranteed found. 3) Identify remaining candidate edge(s) for the missing piece. 4) Run a verification pass to ensure no contradictions with the provided constraints before finalizing.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Assumptions: Standard cube opposites are white-yellow, red-orange, blue-green. I’ll set orientation for reasoning: white on top, green in front, orange on left, red on right, blue at back, yellow at bottom. Constraints to translate: 
- All blue cubies are found ⇒ any edge containing blue is present. 
- All cubes directly touching the orange center (left/right/above/below it) are found ⇒ the four orange-adjacent edges (orange-white, orange-green, orange-yellow, orange-red) are present. 
- Green corners are all present (corners only). 
- All green bordering yellow is present ⇒ the green-yellow edge is present. 
- For all orange cubies found, opposite face’s cubies are found ⇒ edges opposite those orange edges are present on the red face.
I’ll enumerate edge types without blue and not directly adjacent to orange: candidates possibly missing include green-white, green-red, white-red, and red-yellow. We’ll refine with opposites next.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Quick confirmation from standard sources: Opposite color pairs are indeed white↔yellow, red↔orange, blue↔green. Adjacent relationships depend on orientation, but in all standard schemes those opposites hold. No deviations noted.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Map the orange-adjacent found edges to their supposed opposites on red. I’ll pair edges by opposite faces (note: I may be oversimplifying pairs): 
- orange-white ↔ red-white 
- orange-yellow ↔ red-yellow 
- orange-green ↔ red-green 
- orange-red ↔ red-red (center-related, irrelevant for edges)
Given the problem says “for all orange cubes found, the opposite face’s cubes have been found,” this implies those red-edge counterparts are present. Under this pairing, red-white, red-yellow, and red-green are guaranteed found. That leaves green-white, green-red, and white-red as unconstrained. The red-yellow edge is not guaranteed by any non-orange rule, so it’s still a viable missing candidate.

history.name: FileSurfer
history.content: I sketched a textual cube net labeling edges by color pairs under the assumed orientation. Marked as found: all edges with blue; orange-white, orange-green, orange-yellow, orange-red; green-yellow; and the red-face counterparts per the Assistant’s mapping (red-white, red-yellow, red-green). The cells corresponding to red-yellow do not intersect any contradictory constraints in this net. The missing slot candidates narrowed to green-white, green-red, white-red, and red-yellow.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Verification step: We’ll validate a candidate by checking three criteria: 1) It does not include blue (since all blue are found). 2) It is not one of the four edges adjacent to the orange center (since those are found). 3) It is not the green-yellow edge (since that’s found). If a candidate passes all three, we will treat it as consistent with constraints. Testing the candidate red-yellow: it has no blue; it is not adjacent to orange center; it is not green-yellow. It passes all criteria. Based on this validation, we can approve red-yellow as the missing edge.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Applying the approved verification, the removed edge cubie is red-yellow. Alphabetically ordered: red, yellow.

mistake_reason: At step 6, the orchestrator implemented a defective verification procedure that only checked for absence of blue, non-adjacency to the orange center, and not being the green-yellow edge. This ignored the crucial constraint that for all found orange edges, the opposite red edges must also be found. Under correct mapping, red-yellow is guaranteed present (as the opposite of the found orange-white edge). The orchestrator’s verification falsely approved red-yellow by applying inadequate criteria and failing to cross-check opposite-edge relationships, producing a false positive and signing off on an incorrect result. This matches FM-3.3: Incorrect Verification.
